source.author: verg
source.text: Insequitur nimbus peditum clipeataque totis agmina densentur campis, Argivaque pubes Auruncaeque manus, Rutuli veteresque Sicani et Sacranae acies et picti scuta Labici; qui saltus, Tiberine, tuos sacrumque Numici litus arant Rutulosque exercent vomere colles Circaeumque iugum, quis Iuppiter Anxurus arvis praesidet et viridi gaudens Feronia luco; qua Saturae iacet atra palus gelidusque per imas quaerit iter vallis atque in mare conditur Ufens.
source.text_original: Insequitur nimbus peditum clipeataque totis / agmina densentur campis, Argivaque pubes / Auruncaeque manus, Rutuli veteresque Sicani / et Sacranae acies et picti scuta Labici; / qui saltus, Tiberine, tuos sacrumque Numici / litus arant Rutulosque exercent vomere colles / Circaeumque iugum, quis Iuppiter Anxurus arvis / praesidet et viridi gaudens Feronia luco; / qua Saturae iacet atra palus gelidusque per imas / quaerit iter vallis atque in mare conditur Ufens.
source.text_english: A cloud of infantry follows, and shielded ranks pack the whole plain thickly: the Argive youth and the Auruncan troops, the Rutuli and the ancient Sicanians, the battle lines of Sacrana and the painted shields of the Labici; men who till, Tiberinus, your glades and the sacred shore of Numicus, and with the plow work the Rutulian hills and the ridge of Circaeum, where Jupiter Anxurus rules the fields and Feronia, delighting in her green grove; where lies the dark marsh of Satura and where the cold Ufens seeks a course through the lowest valleys and loses itself in the sea.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: quanti enim operantur terram et exercent uomere et tamen multis inpedientibus causis egestate conficiuntur et penuria!
reuse.text_original: quanti enim operantur terram et exercent uomere et tamen multis inpedientibus causis egestate conficiuntur et penuria!
reuse.text_english: For many who till the earth and work with the plow are nevertheless ruined by poverty and want because of many hindering causes!
